title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's mathematics. It is a typed page, page 132, from a manuscript by someone else. It has been photographed upside down, and Grothendieck evidently used the sheet as scrap paper: the neighbouring pages are his handwritten notes on Dieudonné crystals and F/V complexes. The text is the opening of §24, 'Explicit description of pseudo-rational double points'. Section numbering, terminology ('pseudo-rational singularity', 'quadratic transformations', 'Proposition 23.5', 'Corollary 23.3') and subject all match Joseph Lipman's 'Rational singularities with applications to algebraic surfaces and unique factorization' (Publ. Math. IHES 36, 1969), which has a §24 with this title. This is most likely a preprint or typescript version of that paper; I have not checked the typescript pagination.

The mathematics:
- Setting: R is a two-dimensional normal local ring of multiplicity 2 with a pseudo-rational singularity.
- Embedding dimension: the length formula for pseudo-rational singularities (Lipman's §23) gives length(R/m^2) = e + 2 = 4. Hence m/m^2 has dimension 3, so the embedding dimension is 3 and R is a hypersurface 'double point'.
- Programme: classify such R by following them through successive quadratic transformations (blow-ups of the maximal ideal). One asks which conditions on generators x, y, z of m keep every resulting ring normal.
- Converse: conditions of this kind on any local ring force it to be a two-dimensional normal pseudo-rational double point.
- Model case: k[[X,Y,Z]]/(Z^2 − f(X,Y)), i.e. the classical A-D-E / Du Val classification, extended to arbitrary (including mixed or positive) characteristic.

There is no connection to the crystalline material on the surrounding pages beyond physical reuse of the paper.
errors: No mathematical errors attributable to Grothendieck. The typed 'λ(m^2) = 4' is presumably shorthand for the length of R/m^2 being 4 (that is, 1 + embedding dimension 3); read literally, the length of m^2 would be infinite. This reflects the source typescript's notation, not an error on the page.

ideas.what: Classification of two-dimensional pseudo-rational double points (multiplicity 2, embedding dimension 3) via successive quadratic transformations and conditions on generators of m
ideas.modern_name: Rational double points / Du Val (ADE) singularities in arbitrary characteristic
ideas.where_published: Lipman, Rational singularities..., Publ. Math. IHES 36 (1969); not a Grothendieck text

ideas.what: Length formula length(R/m^2) = e + 2 for pseudo-rational singularities, forcing embedding dimension 3 when the multiplicity is 2
ideas.modern_name: Embedding dimension = multiplicity + 1 for rational surface singularities (Artin)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed page of Lipman's rational-singularities manuscript (§24), reused by Grothendieck as scrap paper for his crystal notes. It contains no Grothendieck mathematics, and its content is published (Lipman 1969). The only point of minor archival interest is that Grothendieck had a copy of Lipman's typescript around 1969-70.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down; the transcription correctly reads the rotated text.
The faint handwritten '2' in the corner is the archive page number, not mathematical content.
'λ(m^2) = 4' matches the typescript; mathematically it means length(R/m^2) = 4.
